title: FD vs PPF Calculator
form_description: Compare a lump-sum FD investment against a recurring annual PPF investment over the same period.

clarifier_note.title: Important Clarification
clarifier_note.body: This calculator compares a one-time, lump-sum FD investment with a recurring, annual PPF investment. The 'Annual Investment' amount is invested as a lump sum in the FD at the start, and invested every year in the PPF account.

assumptions.title: Assumptions
assumptions.body:
• FD interest is compounded annually.
  • PPF investment is made at the start of each financial year.
  • Interest rates for both FD and PPF remain constant throughout the tenure.
  • Tax is calculated only on the interest component of the FD at the specified slab rate.

result_snapshot: After {tenure} years, the {winner} yields a higher post-tax return by {difference}.

quick_answer.title: Quick Answer: Which is better, FD or PPF?
quick_answer.body: For long-term goals (15+ years) and for investors in higher tax brackets (20-30%), PPF almost always provides superior post-tax returns due to its EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) status. FDs are better for short-term goals where liquidity is needed and the lock-in periods of PPF are not suitable. Use our tax calculator to determine your slab, and compare with Atal Pension Yojana for guaranteed pension benefits.

how_it_works.title: How the Comparison Works: Worked Examples

example1.title: FD Calculation Example
example1.body:
If you invest â‚¹1,00,000 in an FD for 15 years at 7% interest:

  • Maturity Value = 1,00,000 * (1 + 0.07)^15 = â‚¹2,75,903
  • Total Interest = 2,75,903 - 1,00,000 = â‚¹1,75,903
  • Tax (at 30%) = 1,75,903 * 0.30 = â‚¹52,771
  • Post-Tax Maturity = 2,75,903 - 52,771 = â‚¹2,23,132

example2.title: PPF Calculation Example
example2.body:
If you invest â‚¹1,00,000 every year in PPF for 15 years at 7.1% interest:

  • Your total investment will be â‚¹15,00,000.
  • The final maturity value, through the power of annual compounding, will be â‚¹27,12,139.
  • This entire amount is tax-free.

ppf_features.title: Key Features of PPF
points: Backed by the Government of India, offering highest safety.
EEE status makes contributions, interest, and maturity amount tax-free.
Minimum 15-year lock-in, promoting long-term disciplined savings.
Loan and partial withdrawal facilities available after specific periods.

fd_features.title: Key Features of Fixed Deposit (FD)
points: Flexible tenures ranging from 7 days to 10 years.
Guaranteed returns, not linked to market performance.
Interest earned is fully taxable as per your income tax slab.
Premature withdrawal is possible, though usually with a penalty.

tax_impact.title: The Decisive Factor: Tax Impact
tax_impact.body: The biggest difference between FD and PPF is taxation. Interest from FDs is added to your 'Income from Other Sources' and taxed at your marginal slab rate. For someone in the 30% tax bracket, a 7% FD return effectively becomes just 4.9% post-tax. In contrast, PPF returns are entirely tax-free, making its effective return significantly higher.

checklist.title: When to Choose Which?
points: Choose FD if: You have a short-term goal (1-5 years), need high liquidity, and are in a lower tax bracket.
Choose PPF if: You have a long-term goal (15+ years), are saving for retirement, and are in the 20% or 30% tax bracket.

faqs.question: Can I invest more than â‚¹1.5 lakh in PPF?
faqs.answer: You can deposit more, but the contribution eligible for interest and tax benefits under Section 80C is capped at â‚¹1.5 lakh per financial year.

faqs.question: Is TDS deducted on FD interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, banks deduct TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) at 10% if your interest income from all FDs in that bank exceeds â‚¹40,000 in a financial year (â‚¹50,000 for senior citizens). If you don't provide PAN, the rate is 20%. You may still have to pay additional tax if you are in a higher slab.

faqs.question: Which has a better interest rate, FD or PPF?
faqs.answer: Historically, PPF has offered a higher rate than most bank FDs. Currently, the PPF rate is 7.1%, while most bank FDs for longer tenures are in the 6.5% to 7.25% range. However, the post-tax return from PPF is almost always higher for those in tax-paying brackets.

faqs.question: How does PPF compare with NPS for retirement planning?
faqs.answer: Both PPF and NPS are excellent for long-term savings, but NPS offers market-linked returns with higher growth potential. Use our NPS calculator to compare returns and benefits.

faqs.question: Can I use PPF for child education planning?
faqs.answer: PPF is great for long-term goals like education. For child-specific plans, consider Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana which offers higher interest rates and tax benefits for girl child education.

faqs.question: What about LIC insurance plans vs PPF?
faqs.answer: LIC plans provide insurance coverage along with investment returns. Compare PPF with LIC schemes using our LIC premium calculator and LIC maturity calculator.

conclusion.title: The Right Tool for the Right Goal
conclusion.body: Both FD and PPF are excellent tools in their own right. The choice isn't about which is universally 'better,' but which is better for *your* specific financial goal and timeline. Use this calculator to see the numbers for yourself and make an informed decision that aligns with your financial plan.
